day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response:
Yeah yeah, calm down a second. Let me think.

Donatello what do we actually have here? Food, water, anything useful? Lets assess before we start running around like headless chickens.

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response:
Yeah I got that feeling. Everybody gets that feeling. You´re alive tho so shake it off and make yourself useful, yeah?

Donatello, still waiting on that rundown man.

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response:
Michelangelo come on man, sitting there staring into nothing wont help anyone. Grab whatever you can carry and bring it to Donatello.

Donatello seriously where is that rundown, what are we working with here?

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response:
Alright, logically speaking that´s not a lot. Water is the priority then. We need to find a source before those two bottles run out, everything else is secondary.

DaVinci, you seem like the type to run around anyway so make yourself useful - scout the perimeter, look for any stream or anything wet. Don´t go far.

Donatello, what´s the terrain looking like? We in jungle, mountains, what?

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response:
Good, so swamp south it is. Swamp means water, water means life. Shelter we can figure out later, signal too.

DaVinci still out there scouting? When he gets back we move south as a group. Nobody splits up alone in this terrain, thats just how you die faster.

Michelangelo, you good to walk? Cause we´re moving soon.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: Michelangelo gets one, he looks like he's freezing already. The rest of us sit close to the fire and deal with it. Simple.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response:
I'll go. DaVinci stays here with Michelangelo, keeps the camp running. Two hours on foot is nothing, I can handle that.

But Donatello, this rationing plan - 200ml is barely anything man. We need to move faster on finding that source, not just ration what we have to death. Slow death is still death.

What did you see out there besides the water? Any signs of people, trails, anything?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response:
Wait, I thought I was going to the water source? Make up your mind.

Either way fine, DaVinci and I will sort the camp and the first aid kit. DaVinci you take the shelter, I'll go through the medical supplies and see what we actually have to work with.

Donatello, mark your route back same as you told me. And don't be a hero out there, two hours each way means you're back before dark or we come looking.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response:
Yeah its in the kit, I sorted it this morning. I'll grab it for you.

But hey, while I'm here - that empty bottle next to the rationing plan. You put that there on purpose yeah? Because if Donatello is drinking solo while the rest of us are on 200ml a day that's a problem. A real one.

Don't just sit on that man, say something. Or I will.

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
Crackers too? Alright that´s twice now, that´s not an accident.

Look I get that you don´t want to rock the boat but saying nothing doesn´t make it better, it just means she keeps doing it. When she gets back we address it as a group, calm, no drama. Just lay it out - here´s what we saw, here´s why it´s a problem, done.

You don´t have to be the one to say it if you don´t want. I´ll handle it. But stop sitting on information man, out here that stuff matters.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response:
No man, camp repairs don't wait. We sleep in that shelter tonight, not tomorrow night. Push through it, we can rest when it's done.

Besides I need you sharp and present when Donatello gets back. We've got something to address as a group and I need you focused, not half asleep. I'll tell you about it in a second.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response:
Forget the knot for a second, we've got a bigger call to make.

Food storage gets the patch. I know that sounds cold but hear me out - if the food gets soaked and rots we're done, all three of us. Michelangelo you're sleeping closer to the fire tonight, you'll be warmer anyway and we can rig something temporary over you with whatever scraps are left.

DaVinci, the knot's fine, stop second guessing yourself and start on that patch. Now, before this gets worse.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response:
Yeah exactly, glad we're on the same page. Get it patched fast.

And Donatello, while we're all here - we need to talk. Michelangelo saw you drink a bottle solo and pocket crackers. Both. While the rest of us are on 200ml a day following your own rationing plan. That's not okay, you know that right?

No drama, no lecture. Just don't do it again. We all eat and drink together or not at all. That's the only way this works.
Don't apologize man. Go back to sleep.

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response:
Nah, good thinking. Signal is one of our three priorities anyway, might as well make it visible. Flowers are a bit much but whatever, if it gets us rescued I don't care if you write a poem down there.

Donatello's wrong to dismiss it. Every base covered is one more chance we get out of here.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
Two days to build and a capsize risk. That's not nothing.

Walk me through it - how big are we talking, can it actually hold three people plus supplies, and what's the water situation between here and wherever we're heading? Because if we tip that thing we lose everything and probably drown.

I'm not saying no. I'm saying I need more before I commit to two days of work on something that might kill us faster than staying put. What's your confidence level on this actually floating?

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
Rescue will come. Don't spiral on hypotheticals at 6am on no sleep, that's how you break yourself before anything even goes wrong.

But since you're asking - I think you either get harder or you fall apart. I'd rather get harder. Already halfway there honestly.

Go try to sleep for another hour, we've got a long day ahead if we're seriously considering this raft.

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response: Let him have his space. Not everything needs a response.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response: Ride motorcycles mostly. Clear your head fast when you're doing 140 on an open road, nothing else matters. Gym too. You?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
Five hundred meters is doable if you're a solid swimmer but that's not the part that worries me. What happens if you cramp halfway, or there's a current? Nobody knows you're out there and by the time we notice something's wrong it's too late.

And why the secrecy? If it's a good idea it's a good idea, tell the group. We already had one person making solo decisions with resources and that didn't go great.

I'm not shutting it down but don't go alone and don't go without telling everyone first. That's the deal.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response:
Yeah yeah, I'll get to it. Give me a second.

And for the record I was just finishing up with DaVinci, not slacking. Signal pile gets checked, relax.

Depends what you're doing with it. Logging resources and tasks, fine, useful even. Logging where I was standing at what time and what I was doing every hour? That's a different thing.

What's the notebook actually for Donatello. Be straight with me.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response:
Alright so you're profiling us. Good to know.

Look I get the logic, I do. But if you're sitting on data about who's reliable and who isn't and you're not sharing it, that's the same problem as the crackers. Information hoarded is a liability out here, not an asset.

You want to track patterns, fine. But it's a group resource not a personal one. When you've got something worth saying from that notebook, say it to everyone. Deal?

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
Yeah that's actually smart. Mirror flash can be seen for miles on a clear day, way further than letters on a beach. Good thinking.

Can you actually get one of those panels off clean or are we going to spend three hours fighting with it? Because if it's doable in under an hour it's worth doing today. Let's not overcomplicate it, angle it toward the sun, done.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
day_3.response: Alright man, say it. What's on your mind.

day_3.utterance: I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
Not really. I ride, I lift, I game. Never had much patience for sitting still long enough to learn an instrument. Tried guitar once for about two weeks and got bored.

Why'd you stop the piano?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response:
Nah not really. I just try things and if I'm good I keep going, if I'm not I drop it and find something else. No point torturing yourself over something that doesn't click.

But you stopped piano because you were scared you weren't good enough, not because you didn't like it. That's different. That's just fear man, nothing else.

Anyway - Donatello's right, raft frame needs to get done today. Michelangelo you're with me, let's go. We can talk while we work.

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
*The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
Hey. Hey, come on. One plane means there are more planes. That's how it works.

We've got the SOS on the beach, we've got the mirror panel, we're building a raft. We're not sitting here hoping, we're doing everything right. That plane doesn't erase any of that.

DaVinci pull your head up man. You're the one who drew the SOS this morning, you're the one who got the mirror panel off in twenty minutes. That stuff matters. Don't fall apart now because of one miss.

We move faster on the raft. That's the answer. Less talking, more building. We control what we can control.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
day_4.response: Where? Point it out, don't just stare at it.

day_4.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response:
DaVinci said he saw something glinting near the treeline. That's more important than where he went for five minutes, Donatello.

DaVinci, go check what that is. Don't go alone, take Michelangelo. Shout if it's anything useful.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
That's actually the best news we've had since we crashed. Why are you only saying this now man?

If your family knows the flight path and you've been missing for days, they've called it in. That's what families do. Which means there's probably already a search happening somewhere along that route.

This changes things. We stay visible, we keep the signals up, we push harder on the raft as a backup. But this is genuinely good, not bad. Don't sit on information like that again yeah?

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
Yeah 48 hours is nothing. We've survived this long, we can sit tight for two more days.

Keep the signals up, don't touch the food reserves, finish the raft anyway as backup. And someone feed that fire before it dies completely.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
Yeah I get that. Nobody wants to vanish without a trace.

But you're not disappearing. Your family knows where you are, there's a search happening, and in 48 hours you're going home with a story most people never get to tell. That's not nothing.

The leaving something behind thing though - that's a you problem to solve when you're back home. Piano's still there man. So is everything else you stopped because you were scared. Start there.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response: Pick it up. Answer the radio. Now.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response: Nah you were fine. You kept us alive, that's what mattered.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
Alright, three hours. Let's not sit here doing nothing.

Pack what's worth keeping, leave the rest. Douse the fire properly, don't just kick sand on it. And someone flatten that SOS on the beach so the rescue team knows we're accounted for and not still missing.

Michelangelo get up, you can stare at the sky from the helicopter. DaVinci stop fussing over what to pack, take everything and sort it later.

Donatello, close the notebook. It's done.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
day_5.response: Good. Hold onto that feeling, you're almost there.

Yeah I know. And if we'd hit day five with nothing I'd probably have thanked you for it.

But we didn't. So eat it now, share it, and we call it even. No point carrying guilt onto the helicopter.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
Honestly? Not much. Maybe been quicker to call out the solo resource thing before it became a pattern. And I would've pushed harder on the raft earlier, before the plane scare.

But the big stuff - keeping the group moving, covering all three priorities, not letting anyone fall apart completely - I think that went alright.

What would you change? And be honest, not the clean answer you'd put in a report.

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
Yeah do it. Might actually be useful if this ever happens again to someone.

Send me a copy when it's done. I'm curious what the numbers look like from the outside.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
None. They didn't serve any practical purpose.

But they made DaVinci feel like himself out here, which kept him functional, which kept the group together. Sometimes that's worth more than practical.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response: Yeah I'm good. Just give me a second.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response: Yeah I'm going. Come on, let's move.
